Tokenworks Inc is hiring a Junior Software Developer to build and maintain full-stack products spanning C#/.NET services, TypeScript and Vue front ends, mobile apps, and Azure infrastructure. The role also includes code review, technical specifications, architecture and API design, and product troubleshooting and support.

Responsibilities
Write and ship C#/.NET code for our products
Build and maintain front-end features in TypeScript and Vue
Work across the whole stack — database, web server, network, front end — and understand how the pieces connect
Help maintain and improve our Azure infrastructure
Read and review other people's code, including work from our offshore developers
Contribute to technical specifications, architecture discussions, and API design
Basic troubleshooting and support of our products, in-house and via remote sessions

Work ethic
You're sharp, especially about programming and problem-solving
You're good to work with
We want someone who actually likes this work
Comfort on Linux — you can navigate a filesystem, use Bash, and you're not afraid of a terminal
Working knowledge of Git, ideally from the command line. You understand commits, branches, merges, pull requests, and the difference between a local and a remote repository — and you know that GitHub is not Git
At least one scripting language you're genuinely productive in (Python, Bash, PowerShell, Ruby, or similar)
Real programming ability in at least one language — JavaScript/TypeScript, C#, C, C++, Java, Rust, Go, or something else substantial. Depth in one language beats a résumé listing eight
Evidence that you can build something end to end. A personal project, an internship, coursework you took past the assignment, an open-source contribution — anything we can look at and talk about
Clear written and verbal communication
Authorization to work in the United States
Preferred
Genuine full-stack experience in the original sense of the term — you've integrated a set of software across a network, from database to web server to front end, and made it work
Multiple scripting languages rather than one
Public code we can read: GitHub, GitLab, a blog, anything
A bachelor's degree or higher in computer science, engineering, mathematics, physics, chemistry, or another hard science
